reproduction_target: Genetic-diversity, population-structure and GWAS characterisation of a 169-accession Ethiopian/ILRI subtropical oat (Avena sativa) germplasm panel phenotyped for 21 forage, feed-quality and grain traits across three Ethiopian sites over two seasons. Computational target: GBS read processing and SNP discovery (bcl2fastq v2.20 demultiplexing/adapter trimming -> FastQC -> BWA v0.7.17 alignment to the A. sativa cv. Sanfensan reference (Peng et al. 2022) -> SAMtools v1.15.1 -> NGSEP v4.2.1 variant calling -> call-rate/MAF/PIC/He filtering -> LD-KNNi imputation in TASSEL v5); phenotypic analysis in R v4.3.1 (descriptive statistics, broad-sense heritability/GA/GAM, BLUPs and combined ANOVA via lme4, PCA and hierarchical clustering via FactoMineR/factoextra); genetic-diversity and structure analysis (snpReady He/PIC, MEGA v6.0 Euclidean-distance hierarchical clustering with 1,000 bootstraps, adegenet DAPC over K = 1-40, poppr AMOVA, STRUCTURE v2.3.4 on 1,823 SNPs with 10,000 burn-in / 50,000 MCMC / K = 1-10 / 10 replicates, Evanno delta-K via the web-hosted Structure Selector, marker PCA); LD decay via TASSEL v5.0 with an r2 = 0.2 baseline; GWAS on 18,196 SNPs x 167 genotypes under GLM, MLM, MLMM, FarmCPU and BLINK implemented in GAPIT with an FDR-adjusted p < 0.05 threshold; Manhattan plots via ggplot2; candidate-gene identification in a +/-200 kb window using the Ensembl Plants browser and functional annotation via the OatBioDB web resource (http://www.waooat.cn).
granularity_note: Coarse prose-level decomposition: one step per named tool or named analysis invocation in the Materials and Methods section. Wet-lab and field steps (field trial, phenotyping, NIRS feed-quality prediction, DNA extraction, GBS library preparation and sequencing) are recorded as layer W and scored X (out of scope for computational reproduction). The 23 computational steps form the denominator S. No repository, notebook or script was inspected - this is a prose-only stage-1 read.

steps.label: Wet-lab/field: two-season (2022, 2023) field evaluation of 169 oat accessions (119 EIAR/HARC, 50 ILRI genebank) at three Ethiopian highland sites (Holetta, Adda Berga, Addis Ababa) in a 13x13 partially balanced simple lattice design with two replications, 5.2 m rows at 20 cm spacing, 100 kg/ha seeding rate, 100 kg/ha NPS fertiliser, manual weeding

Wet-lab/field: phenotypic data collection - vigour score, plant height, leaf length, stem thickness, leaves per plant at soft dough stage (mean of five plants), total fresh weight, oven dry weight (60 C, 72 h), derived FTha/DTha, and Marvin seed-analyser grain traits (seed area, width, length, thousand-grain weight)

Wet-lab: NIRS feed-quality prediction (FOSS Forage Analyzer 5000, WinISI II software package) on 1 mm-milled whole-plant/leaf/stem material using a previously developed oat calibration equation following AOAC 989.03; traits ADF, NDF, ADL, OM, DM, ash, N, CP, IVOMD, ME, plus derived MEY
Wet-lab: genomic DNA extraction from freeze-dried young leaf (DNeasy Plant Small Kit, Qiagen) with NanoDrop/DeNovix DS-11 FX quantification and 1% agarose gel integrity check

Wet-lab: GBS library preparation with PstI + ApeKI double digest (LGC Biosearch Technologies protocol) and paired-end 2x150 bp sequencing on an Illumina NextSeq 500/550 v2 system using PstI-ApeKI site-specific primers

Per-lane demultiplexing by sample barcode, adapter trimming, and removal of reads containing ambiguous nucleotides (N), the expected restriction sites, or shorter than 20 bases - Illumina bcl2fastq v2.20
Read quality control and read-count summarisation - FastQC (Andrews 2010; no version stated)
Alignment of adaptor-clipped reads to the A. sativa cv. Sanfensan reference genome (Peng et al. 2022) - BWA v0.7.17
SAM to BAM conversion and downstream file preparation - SAMtools v1.15.1
Variant discovery and SNP calling across 167-169 samples - NGSEP v4.2.1 (Tello et al. 2019); 62,889 raw SNPs reported, 62,221 mapped to the 21 chromosomes

SNP filtering: call rate >= 90% and MAF >= 5% for the analysis set; additional PIC >= 0.2 and He >= 0.2 refinement for the 1,823-marker diversity subset; exclusion of two accessions with >50% missing genotype data - filtering tool/script not named
Imputation of missing genotypes with the LD-based k-nearest-neighbour algorithm (LD KNNi) implemented in TASSEL v5 (Bradbury et al. 2007)

Descriptive statistics (mean, SD, min, max, CV) and genetic variability parameters (broad-sense heritability H2, genetic advance GA, GAM, GCV, PCV) from the stated lattice linear model - R software v4.3.1; no script released

BLUP estimation per trait and combined three-location/two-year ANOVA under the stated mixed model (genotype fixed; year, location, block, replication-within-location random) - lme4 R package (Bates et al. 2015; no version stated) in R v4.3.1

Phenotype-based principal component analysis and hierarchical cluster analysis over 21 traits, with optimal cluster number and membership determination - FactoMineR and factoextra R packages (no versions stated), R v4.3.1; PCA biplots and dendrograms
Per-locus genetic-diversity parameters (expected heterozygosity He, polymorphic information content PIC) - snpReady R package (Granato et al. 2018; no version stated)
Phylogenetic relationships by hierarchical clustering on a Euclidean distance matrix with 1,000 bootstrap replicates - MEGA version 6.0 (Tamura et al. 2013)

Discriminant Analysis of Principal Components (DAPC) with optimal K chosen by minimum BIC over K = 1-40 - adegenet R package (Jombart et al. 2018; no version stated); number of retained PCs/discriminant functions not stated

Analysis of Molecular Variance (AMOVA) partitioning variation among and within clusters - poppr R package (Kamvar et al. 2014; no version stated); permutation count and cluster definition input not stated

Bayesian model-based population structure on 1,823 robust SNPs - STRUCTURE version 2.3.4 (Pritchard 2000) with 10,000 burn-in, 50,000 MCMC iterations, K = 1-10, 10 independent replicates per K; Q > 0.7 assignment threshold, below 0.7 classified admixed
Optimal K inference by the Evanno et al. (2005) delta-K method as implemented in the web-hosted Structure Selector tool (Li and Liu 2018) - externally hosted service, no version or access date stated
Marker-based principal component analysis complementing STRUCTURE - FactoMineR for computation and factoextra for visualisation (no versions stated), R v4.3.1
Pairwise linkage-disequilibrium estimation per chromosome (r2 and associated p-values) - TASSEL version 5.0 (Bradbury et al. 2007) under default parameters
LD decay characterisation: plotting r2 against physical distance in base pairs with an r2 = 0.2 baseline defining linkage equilibrium - R software, package and curve-fitting method not stated

Marker-trait association analysis on 167 genotypes x 18,196 biallelic SNPs (MAF > 5%, missing < 10%) under GLM, MLM, MLMM, FarmCPU and BLINK, significance at FDR-adjusted p < 0.05 - GAPIT in R (Tang et al. 2016; no version stated); kinship/PC covariate settings per model not stated
Manhattan-plot visualisation of -log10(p) against genomic position - ggplot2 in R (Wickham et al. 2016; no version stated); no figure code released

Candidate-gene identification: genes within a 200 kb window upstream and downstream of each significant SNP retrieved from the A. sativa cv. Sanfensan annotation via the Ensembl Plants genome browser - no release/version, no query script

Functional characterisation of candidate genes (gene function, biological pathways, trait relevance) via the Oat Bioinformatics Database OatBioDB (http://www.waooat.cn) - externally hosted service, no version, no access date, no export script

headline.static_readiness: 0/23 (0%) - stage1 ceiling only, no R-star (R-star needs stage-2 code verification)
headline.inference_inclusive_upper_bound: 0/23 (0%) RI, 23/23 NI. Two independent binding constraints, either of which alone would floor the whole pipeline. (1) Data: the entire Data availability statement is 'The data generated and presented in this study is in the process of being deposited in a public database.' No repository is named, no accession number is quoted, and no access date or embargo end is given. Neither the GBS raw reads, nor the called/filtered VCF or HapMap genotype matrix, nor the 21-trait phenotype matrix across three sites and two years is released - the supplementary tables listed in the paper (Sup. Tables 1-6) are accession metadata, trait-definition descriptions and result summaries (ANOVA table, PCA loadings, STRUCTURE and neighbour-joining cluster memberships), not the analysis inputs. Every one of the 23 computational steps therefore scores data = 0. (2) Code: there is no code availability statement at all, and no GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, Zenodo, figshare or Software Heritage identifier appears anywhere in the paper. The only code-shaped URLs in the text are the Babraham FastQC project page cited in the reference list and the third-party web resources Structure Selector and OatBioDB (http://www.waooat.cn). Twelve of the 23 steps (C6, C8-C11, C13, C14, C16, C17, C19-C23) are R-script-driven or web-tool-driven analyses whose code is bespoke and unreleased, scoring code = 0; the remaining eleven are single-invocation runs of well-known command-line tools that a determined reader could reconstruct in principle, scoring code = 1. Version pinning is unusually good for a plant-GWAS preprint - bcl2fastq v2.20, BWA v0.7.17, SAMtools v1.15.1, NGSEP v4.2.1, TASSEL v5/v5.0, MEGA v6.0, STRUCTURE v2.3.4 and R v4.3.1 are all pinned exactly - but eight of the analysis packages carry no version whatever (FastQC, lme4, FactoMineR, factoextra, snpReady, adegenet, poppr, GAPIT, ggplot2), there is no lockfile, renv snapshot, conda environment file or container, and no reference-genome accession or annotation release is given for the A. sativa cv. Sanfensan assembly. Because axis-min governs and data = 0 everywhere, no step can rise above NI regardless of its version quality; the paper's pinning discipline buys nothing until the data are actually deposited. Nothing here is stage-2 recoverable: with no repository to inspect, a code read would add no information.
headline.coverage: 23 of 28 prose-derived steps are computational and in scope (S = 23); 5 are wet-lab/field steps scored X (W = 5). Methods text was read in full from the bioRxiv JATS XML source (https://www.biorxiv.org/content/early/2025/11/27/2025.11.26.690820.source.xml, HTTP 200, retrieved 2026-07-27), including the Data availability statement, Author contribution, Funding, Declarations and Supplementary Tables sections. No repository landing page or README was available to read because no repository is stated.

gaps.where: Data availability statement - all 23 computational steps (C1-C23), entering at C1 from the GBS raw reads
gaps.missing: No public accession of any kind. The complete Data availability statement is, verbatim: 'The data generated and presented in this study is in the process of being deposited in a public database.' The repository is not named (no SRA/ENA/BioProject/NCBI/EBI identifier, no figshare or Zenodo DOI, no dbGaP/EGA controlled-access identifier), no accession number is quoted, no release date or embargo condition is given, and no reviewer-access token is offered. The GBS paired-end reads (2x150 bp, Illumina NextSeq 500/550 v2) that C1-C5 consume, the 62,889-SNP raw call set and the 18,196-SNP filtered GWAS matrix that C6-C7 and C18-C20 consume, and the 1,823-SNP diversity subset that C11-C17 consume, are all unavailable.
gaps.how_to_close: Deposit the GBS FASTQ files under an SRA/ENA BioProject and quote the accession in the Data availability statement; additionally deposit the post-calling VCF, the filtered 18,196-SNP GWAS genotype matrix and the 1,823-SNP diversity subset (with the exact accession-to-sample mapping used) as a versioned Zenodo or figshare record with a DOI.

gaps.where: Whole manuscript - there is no Code availability section; affects all 23 computational steps, and fatally the 12 script-driven steps C6, C8, C9, C10, C11, C13, C14, C17, C19, C20, C21, C22
gaps.missing: No code availability statement exists anywhere in the paper, and no repository identifier (GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, Zenodo, figshare, Software Heritage) is given for any analysis code. The bespoke work is entirely undescribed at the code level: the SNP-filtering step that produces the three distinct marker sets (C6), the heritability/GA/GAM estimation code implementing the stated lattice model (C8), the lme4 BLUP and combined-ANOVA drivers implementing the stated three-way model (C9), all FactoMineR/factoextra PCA and clustering drivers (C10, C17), the snpReady diversity calculation (C11), the adegenet DAPC and poppr AMOVA drivers (C13, C14), the LD-decay plotting and threshold code (C19), the GAPIT driver specifying which covariates each of the five models received (C20), all ggplot2 figure code (C21), and the 200 kb-window candidate-gene extraction against the Ensembl Plants annotation (C22).
gaps.how_to_close: Publish the full analysis code - the SNP filtering pipeline, the R analysis scripts for heritability, BLUP/ANOVA, PCA/clustering, diversity, DAPC, AMOVA, LD decay, the GAPIT driver with its per-model covariate settings, the candidate-gene window extraction, and the figure code - in a public repository with a tagged release archived to Zenodo, and cite the DOI in a Code availability statement. None of this carries any data-embargo risk and it can be released before the data deposit completes.

gaps.where: C2 (FastQC), C9 (lme4), C10 and C17 (FactoMineR, factoextra), C11 (snpReady), C13 (adegenet), C14 (poppr), C20 (GAPIT), C21 (ggplot2)
gaps.missing: Nine analysis packages are cited by name and reference only, with no version number. This matters materially for at least three of them: GAPIT's model implementations and default kinship/PC handling have changed between GAPIT2 and GAPIT3, which can change which of GLM/MLM/MLMM/FarmCPU/BLINK reports a given SNP; adegenet's find.clusters/DAPC defaults and poppr's AMOVA backend have both changed across releases; and snpReady's PIC/He definitions determine the 1,823-marker diversity subset that every structure result depends on.
gaps.how_to_close: State the exact version of every R package used (a sessionInfo() dump pasted into the supplement is sufficient), and pin FastQC's version.

gaps.where: Whole analysis environment - all 23 computational steps
gaps.missing: No environment closure of any kind. R v4.3.1 is pinned but no renv.lock, no CRAN/Bioconductor snapshot date, no conda environment.yml, no Dockerfile, no container image digest, no Apptainer/Singularity definition and no module list for the command-line tools. The operating system, compiler and BLAS/LAPACK backend are not stated, which matters for the MCMC and clustering steps.
gaps.how_to_close: Ship an renv.lock (or a conda environment.yml plus an R package manifest) covering the whole R analysis, and a container image referenced by digest that carries bcl2fastq, BWA, SAMtools, NGSEP, TASSEL, MEGA and STRUCTURE at the stated versions.

gaps.where: C3 (BWA alignment), C5 (NGSEP calling), C22 (candidate-gene window extraction)
gaps.missing: The A. sativa cv. Sanfensan reference genome is cited only as 'Peng et al., 2022'. No assembly accession, no assembly version or patch level, no FASTA checksum, and - for C22 - no Ensembl Plants release number for the gene annotation actually queried. Since Ensembl Plants annotation is re-issued per release, the set of genes falling inside the +/-200 kb windows is not fixed by the prose, and the 46 reported candidate genes cannot be regenerated deterministically.
gaps.how_to_close: Quote the assembly accession and version plus a checksum of the exact FASTA used for C3/C5, and the Ensembl Plants release number (or the downloaded GFF3 with its checksum) used for C22.

gaps.where: C12 (MEGA bootstrap), C13 (adegenet DAPC over K = 1-40), C15 (STRUCTURE 10 replicates per K), C16 (delta-K selection), C10 (hierarchical clustering cut)
gaps.missing: No random seeds are reported for any stochastic step. C15 runs 10 independent MCMC replicates per K with no seed set, C12 runs 1,000 bootstrap replicates with no seed, and C13's find.clusters/DAPC K search over 1-40 involves stochastic k-means initialisation with no seed and no stated number of retained principal components. The determination of the reported K = 2 (and the secondary K = 7) is therefore not bit-reproducible, and the downstream Q > 0.7 assignment of 135 of 167 accessions to Pop1/Pop2 inherits that non-determinism.
gaps.how_to_close: Report the seeds (or the full STRUCTURE mainparams/extraparams files and the MEGA session file), and state the number of PCs and discriminant functions retained in DAPC.

gaps.where: C16 (Structure Selector, Li and Liu 2018) and C23 (OatBioDB, http://www.waooat.cn)
gaps.missing: Two steps depend on externally hosted web services that carry no version, no query record and no access date. Structure Selector performs the delta-K computation that fixes the reported optimal K; OatBioDB supplies the functional annotation and pathway assignment for all 46 candidate genes. Neither service exposes a stable versioned interface in the prose, neither result is archived as a downloadable artefact, and the OatBioDB host is a single non-mirrored domain whose future availability is not guaranteed.
gaps.how_to_close: Archive the exact inputs and outputs of both web queries (the STRUCTURE result archive submitted to Structure Selector and its delta-K output; the OatBioDB annotation export for the 46 candidate genes) as supplementary files with access dates, and additionally compute delta-K locally with a versioned implementation.

gaps.where: Intermediate datasets - the filtered marker sets and the phenotype BLUP table (C6, C7, C8, C9, C20)
gaps.missing: None of the intermediate artefacts that would let a reader re-enter the pipeline downstream of the embargoed raw reads are released: the 62,889-SNP raw call set, the 18,196-SNP filtered GWAS matrix, the 1,823-SNP diversity subset, the per-accession BLUP table, and the GWAS summary statistics for all 21 traits under all five models. Table 2 reports only the selected significant associations (chromosome, position, SNP ID, MAF, allelic effect, detecting model), not genome-wide summary statistics.
gaps.how_to_close: Release the three marker matrices, the BLUP table and the full per-trait per-model GWAS summary statistics as a DOI-bearing deposit. These are derived products and can be released independently of the raw-read deposit.

gaps.where: C3 (BWA), C5 (NGSEP), C20 (GAPIT), C13 (DAPC), C14 (AMOVA), C19 (LD decay)
gaps.missing: Invocation parameters are absent for the steps where they most change the result. C3 does not state which BWA algorithm was used (aln/samse-sampe versus mem) or any mapping-quality filter; C5 gives no NGSEP calling mode, ploidy setting, minimum base/mapping quality or heterozygosity prior, which is consequential for a hexaploid (2n = 6x = 42) genome; C20 does not state which kinship matrix or how many principal components were supplied as covariates to each of the five GWAS models, nor whether the FDR correction was applied per trait or across all traits and models; C13 does not state the number of retained PCs; C14 does not state the permutation count or how cluster membership was supplied; C19 does not state the LD-decay curve-fitting method.
gaps.how_to_close: Publish the exact command lines and configuration files for BWA and NGSEP, the GAPIT call with its covariate arguments, and state the multiple-testing correction scope explicitly.

gaps.where: W3 -> phenotype inputs to C8, C9, C10, C20 (NIRS feed-quality prediction)
gaps.missing: Ten of the 21 analysed traits (ADF, NDF, ADL, OM, DM, ash, N, CP, IVOMD, ME) are not measured but predicted by a proprietary WinISI II calibration described only as a 'previously developed oat equation' following AOAC 989.03. Neither the calibration equation, its coefficients, its training set, its validation statistics, nor the raw NIR spectra are released, and the WinISI II software version is not stated. These predicted values are analysis inputs, not raw observations, so an entire third of the GWAS trait set is generated by an unreleased black box.
gaps.how_to_close: Release the raw NIR spectra and the calibration equation (or its coefficients and validation statistics), and state the WinISI II version, so the predicted trait values can be regenerated.
